title: ENSO strength gave no clear gain in monthly PDO prediction ranges in a 1981-2025 test
abstract: We tested whether ENSO strength improves one-month Pacific Decadal Oscillation prediction ranges beyond seasonal variance. We used fixed NOAA ERSSTv5 PDO and Nino 3.4 snapshots. Models were fit each year on earlier targets from 1951. There were 540 test months in 1981-2025. Both variance models used the same mean prediction with month, recent PDO, recent Nino 3.4 and annual PDO memory. Adding squared Nino 3.4 gave a mean log score gain of -0.00036 nats per month. Its conditional 95% three-year block interval was -0.00993 to +0.00655. Five-year blocks, absolute Nino and removal of annual PDO memory also gave intervals that include zero. Central 90% coverage was 88.33% for the seasonal reference and 88.15% with ENSO strength. This test gives no clear prediction gain. It does not show that ENSO has no physical effect on North Pacific variability. Revised data, a Gaussian variance model and conditional uncertainty limit the result. Code, source hashes, aggregate scores, a figure and separate numerical checks are included. External source tables can be restored from shared snapshots or a cited signed SCI bundle.

display.caption: Adding ENSO strength gave no clear mean log score gain in any planned case. Lines show separate conditional 95% three-year block intervals. Positive gain is better. Yearly primary gains show large losses in some early years.
